content: The Recent Changes page in MediaWiki provides a detailed view of the most recent edits made to pages within a MediaWiki project. This feature allows users to monitor and review the contributions of others, enabling the correction of errors and the removal of vandalism. Links to the Recent Changes page are available at the top of each page and in the sidebar. Users can also create direct links to this page. Each edit is displayed with specific details. For example: The diff link directs users to a page showing the differences introduced by the edit. This link is unavailable for new pages or page moves. The hist link corresponds to the page's history, showing not only the current edit but also older and newer ones. For page moves, this link leads to the history of the new page title. A bold m indicates that the edit was marked as minor by the user. Only logged-in users can mark edits as minor to prevent misuse. A bold page title indicates that the page is unpatrolled. For more information, users can refer to the Help topic on Patrolled Edits. The time of the edit is displayed in UTC, but users can adjust this to their local timezone in their preferences. The number in parentheses (e.g., +100 or -60) shows the change in the article's size in bytes. A positive number indicates an increase, while a negative number indicates a decrease. For logged-in users, links to their user homepage and talk page are provided. For anonymous users, the link directs to their User Contributions page. Users can customize the appearance of the Recent Changes page through their preferences. Options include: Hiding minor edits from the Recent Changes view. Enabling Enhanced Recent Changes, which groups multiple edits together. This feature requires JavaScript and may not work in all browsers. The top of the Recent Changes page displays content from the MediaWiki:Recentchangestext page, which can be edited as needed. Discussions about this content can take place on the MediaWiki talk:Recentchangestext page. Users can view new changes starting from a specific time by using a provided link. This link can be bookmarked or saved for later use. Alternatively, users can manually modify the URL to specify a particular date and time in UTC format. The Special:Recentchanges/hideliu page shows only changes made by users who are not logged in. This feature is useful for monitoring potential vandalism. To combine this with viewing changes from a specific time, users must manually modify the URL to include &hideliu=1. There is a limit of 5000 edits that can be retrieved at once on the Recent Changes page. For longer periods, users can use alternative methods such as: Viewing changes to watched pages using My Watchlist and Revision History. Viewing changes to pages linked from a specific page using Related Changes. Viewing newly created pages using Newly Created Articles. Viewing individual pages or user contributions using Revision History and User Contributions. When a page is renamed (moved), earlier edits, including the original creation, are shown under the new name in Recent Changes. However, if a page is deleted, earlier edits are no longer displayed in Recent Changes. This behavior differs from a true log of editing events, as some actions may no longer be visible after deletion. Bots can be included in the Recent Changes view by adding &hidebots=0 to the URL. Sysops can mark certain edits as bot edits, preventing them from appearing in the default Recent Changes view. For more information, users can refer to the Help topic on Reverting. Patrolling edits is another feature available in MediaWiki. Users can refer to the Help topic on Patrolled Edits for more details. Other MediaWiki features, such as Enhanced Recent Changes and Revision History, provide additional ways to view and analyze edits. The cur and last links in these features allow users to compare the latest edit with the current version or the previous edit, respectively. These links behave slightly differently depending on whether they are used in Enhanced Recent Changes or Revision History.
